name: California (Cal/OSHA)
citation: 8 CCR §3395 Heat Illness Prevention in Outdoor Places of Employment
metric_note: Cal/OSHA §3395 triggers on ambient outdoor temperature, not heat index. A 2 m air temperature feed satisfies it directly.

thresholds.name: Baseline duties (all temperatures)
requirements: Potable water sufficient for 1 quart per worker per hour, located as close as practicable to the work area
Access to shade on request at any temperature
Written Heat Illness Prevention Plan available at the worksite
Employee and supervisor training completed before heat exposure
thresholds.evidence_note: Baseline duties are not temperature-gated. Logged once per shift to keep the record continuous.

thresholds.name: Shade must be present and accessible
requirements: Shade structures erected and open, enough to accommodate all workers on a cool-down rest at one time
Shade located as close as practicable to the work area
Preventative cool-down rest of at least 5 minutes permitted whenever a worker feels the need
thresholds.evidence_note: Shade obligation moves from on-request to must-be-present at this threshold.

thresholds.name: High-heat procedures
requirements: Effective observation of employees for signs and symptoms of heat illness
Effective two-way communication so any worker can contact a supervisor
Designated worker authorised to call emergency services
Pre-shift meeting reviewing high-heat procedures and encouraging water intake
Minimum 10 minute net preventative cool-down rest period every two hours (agriculture)
thresholds.evidence_note: High-heat procedures apply only to the listed industries. This is the threshold most often disputed after a heat-illness claim.

indoor_reference.note: Indoor workplaces reaching 82°F carry a parallel set of duties. Out of scope for outdoor site monitoring but noted so the pack is complete.
